bib.title: MetaICL: Learning to Learn In Context

question: Can meta-training a pretrained LM on many tasks with an in-context-learning objective improve few-shot learning on unseen tasks without templates or parameter updates?
hypothesis: Training on k+1 examples per task in the same format as test-time in-context learning teaches the model to recover task semantics from examples, beating in-context learning without meta-training and multi-task zero-shot transfer.
contributions: MetaICL meta-training framework and a noisy-channel variant
Large-scale evaluation: 142 datasets, seven meta-train/target splits, 52 unique target tasks
Ablations on number and diversity of meta-training tasks, k, model size, and instructions
Code and data released at github.com/facebookresearch/MetaICL

method.summary: Meta-train GPT-2 Large by sampling a task, sampling k+1 examples, concatenating x1,y1..xk,yk,xk+1 and maximising log P(y_{k+1}). At test time condition on k examples and pick the candidate with highest conditional probability; a channel variant models P(x|y).
method.task: few-shot classification and multiple-choice QA/NLI/paraphrase via in-context learning

datasets.name: 142 tasks from CrossFit and UnifiedQA (English)
datasets.size: 142 datasets; meta-train 61 tasks / 819,200 examples in HR; up to 16,384 training examples per task
datasets.split: 7 settings: HR->LR (61 train/26 target), Class->Class (43/20), non-Class->Class (37/20), QA->QA (37/22), non-QA->QA (33/22), non-NLI->NLI (55/8), non-Para->Para (59/4); no task overlap
datasets.source: CrossFit (Ye et al. 2021), UnifiedQA (Khashabi et al. 2020); references in Table 15
datasets.preprocessing: No templates; inputs concatenated, label words from original dataset; one newline between input and output, three newlines between examples (spaces for raw GPT-2); examples truncated to 256 tokens and earlier tokens of concatenation dropped; extractive QA passages truncated keeping the answer for meta-training only

datasets.name: k target training examples
datasets.size: k=16, 5 random sets per target task
datasets.split: sampled uniformly at random, label balance not enforced

other.ablation sizes: small 124M, medium 355M, large 774M, XL 1.5B (XL not meta-trained, memory)

training.objective: negative log likelihood of y_{k+1} given k preceding examples (channel: generate x_{k+1} given y's)

inference.decoding: argmax over candidate set of conditional probability (no generation)
inference.samples: 5 different sets of k=16 training examples per target task; average and worst-case reported, macro-averaged over tasks
inference.prompting: k=16 examples concatenated, no templates or instructions

eval.protocol: Per target task average and worst-case over 5 seeds, then macro-average over target tasks; reported on all targets and on targets with no domain overlap with meta-training. No significance test stated.

limits: In-context approaches need much longer context at meta-training and inference
Only a causal LM of modest size (GPT-2 Large, 770M) tried; masked LMs and larger models left to future work
Only classification and multiple-choice tasks with a candidate set; free-form generation not covered
Fine-tuning with meta-training still beats MetaICL
Direct comparison with Wei 2022 and Sanh 2022 is hard: model size, LM type, and splits differ
Variance across choices of meta-training tasks is non-negligible
Performance with random label words is relatively poor

terms.definition: Meta-training for In-Context Learning: a pretrained LM is tuned on a large set of training tasks to do in-context learning

lineage.work: Language models are few-shot learners (Brown et al.)
